name: the Oasis
line: Trees - real trees, green under a grate's light - stand in a ring about a pool, and the air is sweet. Something glints on the far bank, and something under the water.

name: the Bone Room
line: Bones, heaped against every wall to the height of a man, and the floor black with their dust. One heap is bigger than any beast you know. Something is not all here.

name: the Hall of Doors
line: A long hall, and doors down both its walls - more doors than any hall needs. Most of them, you would guess, go nowhere.

name: the Fish Pool
line: A pool fills the room wall to wall, black and still, and something moves in it - fish, small and quick. A line of planks runs out to a stone in the middle, and a chest on the stone.

name: the Garden Gone Wild
line: Beds in rows, a well, a bench gone to moss: a garden someone kept down here, under a grate's light, and the plants have had it to themselves a long time.

name: the Chapel of Candles
line: Candles in rows, every one of them lit, and no one here to have lit them. The altar at the end is warm.

name: the Map Room
line: A stone table fills the middle of the room, and cut into its top, worn by many hands: the floor you stand on, every hall of it.

name: the Rookery
line: The roof goes up out of the torchlight, and something up there shifts and chitters - a great many somethings. The floor is soft with their leavings.

name: the Cistern
line: A sunken hall with a drain in every wall: the town's cistern, dry today. After a storm above it would stand to the waist, and the chest in the middle would be a dive.

name: the Dripping Gallery
line: A long gallery under the street: the drip of it from the roof in a dozen places, puddles on the floor, moss on everything. Something glints in one of the puddles.

name: the Storm Drain
line: A channel runs through the room, stone-lined, and water in it; after rain above it would run fast. A sluice gate stands at one end.

name: the Steam Room
line: Hot stone, and a pool in the floor that would be boiling if it were not fed from the cold above. Under a winter sky this room is a white blindness.

name: the Lightning Rod
line: An iron rod runs from a grate in the roof to the floor, pitted and black. In a storm above it would sing - and anything that lives on lightning would come to it.

name: the Echo Chamber
line: Every step comes back twice off the walls. A bell hangs in the middle of the room on a frayed rope, and you would not want to be the one who rings it.

name: the Gauntlet
line: A long run of floor, and every other flag of it pierced: the vents breathe in turn, a beat apart. Something at the far end is worth the burns.

name: the Weighing Room
line: A great brass scale stands in the middle of the room, and on one pan something that shines. The other pan is empty, and it waits.

name: the Barrow
line: A long mound under a low roof, steps cut up its side to a stone coffin on the top. Grave goods lie at its foot, and the lid is carved with a story.

name: the Wolf Den
line: Roots come down through the roof here, and trees with them, and in the middle a ring of grey shapes asleep round a kill. Their breath is slow.

name: the Troll Bridge
line: Black water either side, a long way down, and one narrow bridge across it. Halfway along, something large sits with its feet over the edge, and turns its head.

name: the Painter's Room
line: An easel, a stool, a palette with the paint still wet, and on the canvas the party - all of you, half done. The painter's hand is still on the brush. The painter is not.

name: the Orrery
line: Brass rings in the floor, one inside the next, and on them the sun, the moon and the wandering stars on arms, and the whole of it turning, slow, with the sky you cannot see.

name: the Lich's Study
line: A desk, a chair, a lamp long out, and papers everywhere in a hand you have seen cut into the walls. This is where he worked it out.

name: the Kitchen
line: A kitchen: the oven cold, the knives on the wall, the flour bins open, and in the flour, a great many small footprints. The bread recipe is carved beside the door.

c.note: on the wall: the cook's knives

name: the Mirror Hall
line: Two rows of pillars down a long room, and at the far end a mirror taller than a man in a black frame. Your own lights come down the hall to meet you in it.

name: the Cold Store
line: The cold comes out to meet you at the door. Frost on every wall, meat on hooks along them, and at the back, on a step of ice, something that was put here to keep too.

name: the Tilting Floor
line: A square room with a chest in the middle of it, and four plates in the floor about the chest, worn by feet. The whole floor rings hollow underfoot.
sealed: held down by a stone bar, till the plates are stepped in their order

name: the Puzzle of Lamps
line: Five lamps on the far wall, all of them out, and a carving under them in the old hand. There is a draught from somewhere that is not the door.

name: the Spider Hollow
line: Webs from floor to roof in every corner, thick as sailcloth. Shapes hang in them, wrapped; round sacs, grey and soft, stand along the floor; and up on a ledge, something waits with its legs drawn in.

name: the Kennel
line: Iron cages along both walls, and the smell of iron and dog. Half the cages have something in them, and it has heard you. A lever stands by the far wall, and a hook beside it.

name: the Hall of Fame Annex
line: Plaques on the walls of a small square room, a bell in the middle, and a chest at the far end. The names on the plaques are names you know, because you gave them.
sealed: its lid held fast, till the bell is rung for them

name: the Giant's Ribcage
line: A colossus fell here, or was laid here, and the hall was cut round its bones: the ribs go up over you in two rows and meet under the roof, and at the far end a skull the size of a cart looks back down the hall with something between its teeth.

name: the Shipwreck
line: A ship came down through the vault's roof, stern first, and lies broken in the black water with its mast still up. The Drowned stand on the deck in a row, as still as the mast, and the water laps at the hull.

name: the Rope Bridge
line: The floor stops. Across a dark that goes down farther than your light, one bridge of planks and rope, and at its far end, something on a rope of its own.

c.note: hauled up on a rope from under the bridge's end

name: the Great Mushroom
line: One mushroom, as wide as the hall, on a stalk you could not reach round, its cap up under the roof with glowcaps burning at its foot. Steps are cut into the stalk. Under the cap, something small breathes slow.

name: the Fallen Star
line: The floor is broken in a ring, the flags thrown up round a hollow, and in the hollow something dark and pitted that is not stone, with a heat coming off it you feel on your face. A star came down through forty floors of rock to lie here.

name: the Waterfall Hall
line: The aquifer comes through the far wall in a sheet and goes down roaring into a pool, and the spray is on everything. Behind the sheet, the wall is not all wall.

name: the Lantern Shaft
line: A small square hall with a grate in its roof, and up through the grate a shaft that goes on and on, and at the top of it a coin of sky. The light comes down it in a column, and the weather with it. A rope ladder goes up to a ledge.

c.note: on the ledge, where the rope ladder goes

name: the Sunken Chapel
line: A chapel with the water up to the fourth pew: the near half dry, the far half under black water with the benches still standing in it. Something under the water, in the middle, has the shape of a bell.

name: the Petrified Wood
line: Trees, stone to the last leaf, and between them a deer with its head up, stone, and a man with his hand out, stone. There is a fountain. Whatever did this to them has not gone far.

name: the Throne of the Hollow One
line: A throne grown out of the root itself, and on it a shape with a crown on its head, asleep or near enough. The roots go out across the whole floor from the throne's foot, as if the hall were its hand.

name: the Hourglass Room
line: A glass the height of a man in a brass frame in the middle of the room, all its sand in the bottom bulb, and four chests against the walls with their lids held down by bars. The frame has a handle, and the glass turns.
sealed: held by a bar that lifts while the sand runs

name: the Riddle Gallery
line: A gallery crossed by three walls, and in each wall a door with a statue standing in it - a hooded shape with a hand up. The hand says: wait. The mouth, when you come near, says more.

name: the Pendulum Hall
line: A hall one flag wide between two pits, and across it, on a beat you can count, blades on chains sweep the width of the way and back. There is a chest at the far end, and a rhythm to learn.

name: the Dark Room
line: The torch goes out at the door, and will not take again while you stand in here. It is not a draught. The dark has a shape to it, and the shape is asleep in the middle, and the way on is the far wall.

name: the Frozen Pond
line: The floor is ice from wall to wall, black and clear with the dark under it, and out on it three islands of stone with something on each. A step onto the ice is a long step.

name: the Wind Tunnel
line: The draught comes down the hall like a hand on your chest, and the torch goes to nothing in it. Along the walls the air is still. Down the middle, it is not.

c.note: in the eye of the wind

name: the Counting Room
line: Gold on the floor: not a chest of it, the floor itself, coin on coin, wall to wall, and an altar in the middle with a plate on it, and an iron gate drawn up over the door you came in by. The Counting-House's cousin, and its rule is cut on the altar: take what you like. Leave what you must.

name: the Crawlway
line: The roof comes down to your shoulders and stays there: a room you cross bent double, with the breath of something small and many in it, and a chest so low you could step over it.

name: the Weighing of Deeds
line: A scale, but no pans: two hands of stone held out, and between them a thing of the band's that shines. The carving under it says the scale weighs not gold but what you have done, and gives or does not.

name: the Dice Room
line: A stone die the size of a stool in a box of its own, a painted board on the wall with a six and a one on it, and a chest with its lid barred. The Joker's room, or one of his friends'. The stake is fifty.
sealed: barred till the die shows six

name: the Rat King's Nest
line: Rags and bones and the smell, and rats - on every flag, in every corner, going over one another - and in the middle a nest of what they have dragged in, and on it one of them, bigger, with something on its head that shines.

name: the Hatchery
line: Warm sand underfoot, and the heat coming up through it, and in the sand, in a ring, eggs the size of a man's chest, leathery and grey and one of them rocking. Overhead a shaft goes up into the dark, and something up there breathes.

name: the Bandit Camp
line: A fire in the middle of the hall and four about it with their backs to the walls and their hands near their hilts, and behind them a pile of what they have taken off the people who came this way before you. They have seen you. They are deciding.

c.note: the bandits' pile, behind the fire

name: the Vampire's Parlour
line: A parlour: a long table laid for guests who are not here, candles burning that no one lit, a mirror that shows the room and not you, and at the table's head a chair with someone in it, very still, who smiles.

name: the Golem Forge
line: A slab, and on it a golem of crystal half made - the legs and the trunk and one arm, the rest in pieces on the floor beside it - and a lever by the furnace mouth that someone did not pull. The vents breathe round it.

name: the Drowned Shrine
line: Water to the knee, and in it a ring of the Drowned on their knees with their faces down, and in the middle a stone the sea shaped, and on the stone a pearl. They have not looked up. They are waiting for something to be put on the stone.

name: the Chronicle Wall
line: A long wall painted in panels, and the panels are you: every time a party of this house came down this shaft, who they were and how far they went and how it ended, in a painter's hand that was not told any of it.

name: the Old Camp
line: A camp: the ring of stones and the ash in it cold, a tent gone to rags, a pot, and a note weighted with a stone. Someone of this house slept here, on this seed, and did not come back up.

name: the Festival Hall
line: A hall dressed for a feast - for which feast you can tell by the dressing, and the table in the middle is laid, and the chest at its head has its bar down. Come on the day, says the carving over the door, and the bar lifts.
sealed: barred till the festival's own day

name: the Smuggler's Drop
line: A small room with nothing in it but a door in the far wall that does not open, and a mark cut low in the frame that someone in the Square would know. Behind it, a cache.
